result: A stable-manifold theorem for time-varying dynamics shows that gradient descent, mirror descent, proximal point and manifold descent with vanishing steps of order Ω(1/k) avoid strict saddles from almost every start; steps that shrink too fast (summable) can stop at non-critical points.
result_plain: GD and relatives with vanishing Omega(1/k) steps avoid strict saddles almost surely; summable steps may stall at non-critical points.
